newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bunker market beat out by foreign hubs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bunker market beat out by foreign hubs.

text.p: North American bunker prices were slighty higher to unchanged early this week as weaker pricing abroad lures away business, players said on Tuesday.
Both the East and West Coasts traders reported slim volumes as many shipowners sailed to European and Far East hubs to buy fuel.
"We are going to have to come down soon to attract any business," said an East Coast trader.
In New York Harbor, spot 380 CST was up $1 a tonne from last Thursday to between $97 and $99 a tonne, with 180 CST at $103/104.
Rotterdam bunkers were quoted, however, as low as $86, mostly by majors.
Houston 380 CST on the Gulf Coast was also up $1 to remain on par with the Harbor.
On the West Coast, Los Angeles markets were also losing business to the Far East where in some ports such as Singapore bunkers were selling $10 to $15 less.
Los Angeles 380 CST was steady at $105/106 a tonne, and 180 CST was $110/111.
